newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH RABOBANK TO KEEP COOP STATUS INTO NEW CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH RABOBANK TO KEEP COOP STATUS INTO NEW CENTURY.

text.p: Dutch bank Rabobank Nederland said it planned to retain its cooperative status as it headed into the next century.

Executive board chairman Herman Wijffels said that during recent talks with senior management, the bank's 4,000 local board governors had agreed to the mutual structure remaining in place into the new millennium.

"We will have to finally decide that in the course of this year. Factually that decision has been made but formally it's still to be ratified in the course of this year," he told Reuters after a news conference for the bank's 1996 results.
Wijffels noted that many mutual organisations around the world had changed to company status and listed on the sharemarket in recent years, including British building societies.
Rabobank, the third-biggest Dutch bank after ABN AMRO and ING Groep , has to rely on internally generated funds for growth as it has no shareholders from which to raise new capital.
The bank earlier said it had decided to syndicate and securitise loans in an attempt to limit lending growth, which otherwise pressures its strong capital ratios.
